key_insight: Instead of predicting absolute MOS, the paper reframes IQA as a relational, directional task: a model learns which image is more distorted and where, using synthetic, self-supervised distortions to train without human labels.
problem_solved: Eliminates costly and coarse mean-opinion-score collection and provides interpretable, localized feedback about specific image distortions for downstream tasks.
method: Synthetic distortion engine generates diverse, spatially-aware corruptions and controlled pairs/triplets for self-supervised training.
A distortion-prediction network is trained to produce directional/relational judgments and pixel-level distortion maps (where and which image is worse) rather than absolute MOS.
Learning objective leverages pairwise/relative supervision and spatial consistency to produce interpretable, localized quality estimates.
impact: Enables scalable, annotation-free training of IQA models that give per-pixel, actionable feedback—useful for image restoration, compression, and model auditing—while improving interpretability and reducing labeling cost.

paper_title: Pixel Perfect: Relational Image Quality Assessment with Spatially-Aware Distortions
paper_authors: Fadeel Sher Khan, Long N. Le, Abhinau K. Venkataramanan, Seok-Jun Lee, Hamid R. Sheikh
